conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I understand your dialysis line came loose today. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it pulled out a bit at daycare. I was moving around and suddenly felt it shift. They couldn’t get any IV access, so they sent me here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You’ve had trouble with access before. We’ll need to fix the line. Interventional radiology will replace it under light sedation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that safe? Last time I had a line infection with MRSA.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re aware of your history. The team will use sterile technique, and we’ll monitor closely. No signs of infection now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The procedure is done. They replaced your left subclavian dialysis line successfully. A midline was placed to help with sedation access.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. Can I eat now? I’ve been NPO since yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you can start eating. We’ll get you something soon. You also had dialysis earlier and they removed about 3 liters of fluid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I’ve been feeling swollen in my legs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We noticed some pitting edema. Your dry weight is 84.7 kg, and you were over that. Dialysis helped bring your blood pressure down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been trying, but sometimes I forget to check my weight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s important to weigh yourself daily. Call your doctor if you gain more than 3 pounds in a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We checked your labs last night. Your potassium was a bit high at 5.7, but dialysis corrected that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I change my diet?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep avoiding high-potassium foods like bananas and oranges. Your other labs are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nursing also noted pressure ulcers on your left gluteal area. They’re not infected, but you’ll need wound care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I sit on my scooter a lot. Should I change how I sit?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, reposition every 30 minutes. Avoid putting all your weight on the left side. A home health nurse will help with wound care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re clearing you to go home. Your line is working, and you’re stable after dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Are my medications the same?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, no changes. Keep taking oxycodone for hip pain, gabapentin, Keppra, and all your other meds as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And dialysis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resume your regular schedule. The center will contact you. Make sure you’re home on time for visits.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. Sometimes I lose track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’re referring you to a new service to help with that. It’s important for your care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your midline was removed earlier. The dialysis line is secure and ready for use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I feel better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and follow up with your doctors. We’ll see you if anything changes.
